texts.preamble: I.M.Selvaraj vs / on 3 December, 2024 W.P.(Md) No.2 Before The Madurai Bench Of Madras High Court Dated: 03.12.2024 Coram: The Honourable Mr.Justice K.Kumaresh Babu W.P.(Md) No.23887 of 2017 and W.M.P.(Md) Nos.20021 and 20022 of 2017 I.M.Selvaraj ... Petitioner /vs./ 1.The Food Safety Officer, Code No.576, O/o. Designated Officer, Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration Department, Viswanathapuram Madurai -14, Madurai District. 2.The Adjudicating Authority, The District Revenue Officer, Madurai District. ... Respondents Prayer: Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of In issuance of Writ of Certiorari, calling for the records relating to the proceedings in Na.Ka.C6/70791/16 pending before the 2nd respondent and the same. 1/6 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.(Md For Petitioner : Mr.R.Parthiban For R1 : Mr.R.Suresh Kumar Additional Government Pleader For R2 : No appearance I.M.Selvaraj vs / on 3 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116359148/ 1 Order
texts.arguments: The challenge in the writ petition is to the show cause notice issued by the second respondent based upon the report on the factual premise that the product sold by the petitioner did not meet the standards of a food product. 2. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that what the petitioner had sold was Gingelly Lighting Oil and the same cannot be used for consumption. The label of the bottle had also indicated that the same was not recommended for cooking purposes and is for external use. When that be so, the entire proceeding initiated against the petitioner is wholly without jurisdiction, as the product of the petitioner at any stretch of imagination will not fall under the definition of food as defined under Section 2(j) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (herein after referred to as FSSAI Act, 2006). Hence, he would seek to quash the impugned order. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3. The learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for the first respondent would submit that the lighting oil was minutely written, which would mislead the consumers to treat it as a Gingelly Oil and to use for cooking purposes. He would further submit that the label had also contained that the product contained sesame oil, Palmolein Oil and Refined Rice Bran Oil. When that be so, there has been a misbranding of the product. Hence, the same would fall within the mischief of Section 23 of FSSAI Act, 2006 and Regulations framed therein relating to packaging and labeling. Therefore, he would seek this Court to dismiss this writ petition.
